title: Clinical model distinguishes selected rare-infection diagnoses in archived admissions
summary: HistGradientBoosting used early-admission clinical records to distinguish a selected composite of rare infections from urgent-admission controls. The primary holdout table reports an ROC area of 0.937; a separate comparative validation table reports mean sensitivity of 61.9%. This is internal retrospective evaluation, without demonstrated earlier diagnosis or clinical benefit.

source_review.scope: Original primary clinical/computational Methods, model evaluation and high-level Results read; no operational biological protocols

evidence.ai_role: A fitted boosted-tree classifier maps early clinical and laboratory features to chart-confirmed diagnostic labels; SHAP describes model-used features.
evidence.tested: The study used1494 cases and10000 sampled controls from2010–2023, with a70:30 patient split. Training-only cross-validation, SMOTE and isotonic recalibration are described. The paper distinguishes a448-case/3001-control test composition.
evidence.unknown: The abstract and cross-validation table report AUC0.947 while the separate holdout/ablation table reports0.937; these are retained as different reported evaluations, not silently equated. Early predictor timing does not prove predictions preceded actual diagnosis. The selected six-disease composite and sampled-control prevalence limit calibration and clinical transfer. Supplementary inclusion details were not read. No pathogen methods, treatment protocol, real-world alert deployment or prospective outcome benefit is represented. The 61.9% sensitivity comes from the comparative validation table, not an authenticated operating point for the separate holdout AUC of 0.937.
